claim: Pressing Stop during a SettlementForge creation's history replay has no defined outcome in host mode. - **How a host creation runs.** The module runs `generate(blueprint, { docId: mapId, prefix })` inside a `dossier.offer { create }` (V08 §3.3, l.1536-1543), and every editing client's creation must be byte-identical (T-V8-3; V08 W10). A dossier carrying a history makes it a history-first generation (V08 §3.15). - **What V09 offers.** V09 §4.21.9 (1)–(2) (l.3398-3420) shows the progress view, with **Stop** for "item 113's history replay at generation, through `generate`'s `signal`". It says nothing of host mode. A stopped history-first generation "leaves no document and shows `info.history.cancelled` with **Generate without its history**" (V06 §3.20.4, l.3148-3149; T-V9-79). - **What happens in host mode.** `OfferStatus` (V08 l.383) has no cancelled status. So, read as written: - the host gets no `dossier.result` until its 60 s `replyTimeoutMs`; - V08 §3.9's B2 then re-creates the frame and re-runs the whole creation; - "Generate without its history" would make a document with `history.replay` false, which no other editor's creation equals (T-V8-3), against the history the dossier supplies (item 113). - **The alternative reading** — the host's `generate` call passes no `signal`, so it shows no Stop — is stated nowhere.
